- When sentiment is positive (≥0.20) and forecast is rising, reduce forecast slope to avoid over-optimism.  
- If recent history shows sharp upward moves followed by model overestimation, apply a 5–10% downward correction to next period.  
- If true outcome exceeds forecast by >5% for 2+ consecutive days, assume momentum bias and adjust future forecasts downward.  
- When sentiment is neutral or negative (≤0.00) and forecast is rising, cap upward movement at 1–2% above recent high.  
- If forecast is flat or declining but true outcome spikes upward, assume sentiment shift — adjust forecast upward by 2–5% of spike magnitude.  
- For 30-day horizon, if forecast is consistently > true outcome by 3–5% over 3+ periods, apply mean reversion bias correction.  
- If sentiment history shows no positive sentiment but true outcome spikes, assume market surprise — reduce forecast slope by 10–15% for next 3 periods.
